justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: SFU Media Relay handles video consultations, Backend Service and Integration Adapter manage e-prescriptions, AI Symptom Checker Service handles triage, and Consent & Policy Service enforces consent management.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance is addressed thoroughly via PgBouncer connection pooling, Memorystore for Redis caching, Symptom Session Cache, Envoy Compression Filter, and ABR Controller for adaptive video streaming over constrained connections.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is thoroughly addressed by the Integration Adapter Container, featuring the FHIR Translation Component for US HIEs and EU National e-Prescription Adapter for European pharmacy networks over mTLS.
justifications.usability: While the ABR Controller provides degraded video for rural patients, user-facing client applications (e.g., patient mobile apps, clinician portals) are omitted, showing users connecting directly to the infrastructure load balancer.
justifications.reliability: Reliability is well addressed: ABR Controller maintains consultations below 300 kbit/s, while Envoy provides circuit breaking, rate limiting, and active health checks across GCP regional backends.
justifications.security: Security is thoroughly designed with Google Cloud Armor, Istio mTLS, OPA consent enforcement, Payload Sanitizer & PII Redactor, Cloud KMS regional envelope encryption, and WORM storage for MDR audit logs.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture exhibits clean modularity, separating concerns into autonomous containers and components like the Integration Adapter Container and Consent & Policy Engine, enabling isolated maintenance and regional extensions.
justifications.portability: Target GCP regions (europe-west3, us-central1) are explicitly targeted using GKE containers. However, heavy reliance on GCP-specific services (Cloud Armor, Cloud SQL, Memorystore, GCS WORM) limits cross-cloud portability.

PERF-01.justification: The SFU Media Relay, Redis session caching, and Envoy gateway enable rapid connection setup, but horizontal auto-scaling and clustering details for handling 5,000 concurrent media streams are not fully articulated.
sensitivity_points: Signaling and session handshake latency in Redis cluster
tradeoffs: Centralized session verification vs. connection setup latency

PERF-02.justification: The Symptom Session Cache and FastAPI routing provide fast local execution, but response latency remains heavily dependent on external third-party AI inference providers.
sensitivity_points: External AI inference endpoint latency and rate limits
tradeoffs: Inline PII redaction overhead vs. strict privacy compliance

AVAIL-01.justification: The SFU Media Relay includes a dedicated ABR Controller for localized degradation on low-bandwidth rural connections, while consultation state and clinical notes remain decoupled in the backend.
sensitivity_points: Threshold sensitivity of the ABR Controller under packet loss
tradeoffs: Lower video resolution to maintain continuous audio and session stability

AVAIL-02.justification: Only two target regions (us-central1 and europe-west3) are provisioned. If us-central1 suffers a total regional outage, US patients cannot be served without violating data residency constraints or failing over to an unmodeled secondary US region.
elements: GCP Global HTTPS Load Balancer with Geo-routing
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (Enterprise Plus Edition)
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary regional disaster recovery deployment in the US
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents cross-region failover to EU during outages

MOD-01.justification: The integration layer explicitly isolates national prescription protocols into dedicated adapters (EU National e-Prescription Adapter using Apache Camel), allowing changes to be localized without affecting core backend services.
sensitivity_points: Interface consistency between translation components and national gateways
tradeoffs: Adapter translation complexity vs. core clinical domain stability

MOD-02.justification: The architecture explicitly captures model versions and inputs via the AI Traceability & Logging Interceptor and writes immutable audit logs to GCP Cloud Storage WORM, while the Region-Aware Model Router handles version routing.
elements: GCP Cloud Storage with Object Retention (WORM)
sensitivity_points: Atomic logging of model identifiers with inference requests
tradeoffs: Storage retention overhead vs. EU MDR auditability and compliance

SEC-01.justification: Cross-region requests are routed via secure gRPC channels and intercepted by Open Policy Agent (Consent & Policy Engine) to verify consent before data retrieval, with all events logged.
sensitivity_points: Policy evaluation latency during inter-regional mTLS token validation
tradeoffs: Strict real-time consent checks vs. cross-border access performance

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates in Cloud SQL are immediately evaluated by OPA to block access, and changes are audited. However, specific asynchronous batch data-pipeline revocation mechanisms for pre-shared research extracts are not explicitly described.
elements: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (Enterprise Plus Edition)
sensitivity_points: Cache invalidation latency for cached consent policies in Redis
tradeoffs: Instant query-time policy evaluation vs. batch data purging overhead
